items.title: Despite calling Grand Theft Auto 'a videogame franchise built around criminal activity,' Miami-Dade sheriff isn't mad about the NBA's 'Vice City' transformation
items.summary: Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz says her strong stance against the GTA 6 promotional collaboration was only about

content.v: THEN:
NOW:
WHAT?

Vice City and Leonida, the fictional city and state that serve as the setting for Grand Theft Auto 6 , are largely based on Miami and the state of Florida, and Rockstar and publisher Take-Two Interactive are moving heavy and hard to leverage that real-life inspiration to promote GTA 6 as its console release gets closer.

The sheriff made no bones about her position on the matter when the proposed partnership came to light in September, however, characterizing the game as exactly the sort of thing Miami-Dade shouldn't associate with.

"Grand Theft Auto is a videogame franchise built around criminal activity," Cordero-Stutz said at the time. "Its fictional world includes murder, robbery, drug trafficking, carjacking, violence against law enforcement, and other conduct that the men and women of the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office work every single day to prevent."

It was a hard line in the sand, but it didn't add up to much. Despite some opposition from local positions, much of it predicated on similar law-and-order concerns, those PR campaigns have moved ahead. The City of Miami Beach voted in September to approve a 'discreet' campaign , for instance, while the Kaseya Center, a downtown arena in Miami that serves as home of the NBA's Miami Heat, took a rather less subtle approach, erecting a massive " Welcome to Vice City " sign on its roof that can be seen by travellers flying into Miami International Airport.

The Kaseya Center campaign became even more prominent in October when the Heat, one of the NBA's highest-profile teams, became directly involved via the Night in Vice City campaign, a one-night-only promotion that will see both the arena and the team rebranded in Vice City livery. It is, as former US President Joe Biden once said , "a big fuckin' deal."
A post shared by Miami HEAT (@miamiheat)
A photo posted by
(It also revealed that our UK team does not know ball , but that's a whole different kind of problem.)

I thought the sheriff might take issue with such a high-profile embrace of a videogame she had so wholeheartedly decried just a month ago, Despite her previously-expressed opposition, though, she seemingly has no issue with the Heat hopping on board.

"Sheriff Cordero-Stutz’s comments focused on the proposed use of publicly owned facilities and infrastructure, including public transportation, transit stations, and Miami International Airport, to promote Grand Theft Auto 6," a sheriff's department representative told PC Gamer. "Her concerns addressed the message conveyed through the use of these public assets. Those comments were not directed at promotional decisions by private businesses or organizations."
We're not giving away pistols and cocaine to people
Miami Beach Commissioner Monica Matteo-Salinas, arguing in favor of GTA 6 collab

I'm not sure how much of a difference the public/private thing makes in a practical sense—public or private, 'Miami is becoming Vice City' is the very high-profile crux of the campaign—but in spite of the many years passed since the Hot Coffee scandal , it's a needle that some are still trying to thread. The promo campaign approved by Miami Beach, for instance, will be managed by Boucher Brothers, a "hospitality management" company in Florida: Advertising materials will appear on things like Boucher Brothers chairs and umbrellas, rather than on city property.

Those chairs and umbrellas may appear on city property, which makes me think that trying to put some sort of minimum safe distance between them and the responsibilities of civic leadership might be largely moot.

On the other hand, the outright alarmism of days past has clearly receded. The glitzy rebranding of Miami and other parts of Florida speaks for itself, and Cordero-Stutz's admonishment notwithstanding, police don't seem too worried that pretending to be Vice City is going to turn Miami into actual Vice City: During the Miami Beach debates, for instance, one city commissioner said an officer he spoke to laughed off concerns about the impact of the game and promotional campaign on the city. Crass commercialism isn't really my bag but as someone who was around for the entire Jack Thompson era, I have to admit that this is kind of nice to see.

items.title: 《最终幻想 7：启示录》温泉场景揭晓派对新泳衣皮肤
items.summary: New Final Fantasy 7 Revelation footage has revealed a hot springs feature that boosts the party's health and g

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/05/final-fantasy-7-revelation-hot-springs-1791226316325.png
New Final Fantasy 7 Revelation footage has revealed a hot springs feature that boosts the party's health and gives them a set of new bathing suit skins.

Half the fun of Square Enix's remake trilogy is allowing Cloud, Barret, Tifa, and the rest of the party to have some fun on their way to stop Sephiroth once and for all. In Rebirth , that meant spending a day at the beach , and in Final Fantasy 7 Revelation, players will be able to kick their feet up, mingle, and, for some reason, balance rubber Chocobos at a collection of new hot springs.

The publisher unveiled the new gameplay feature as part of SDCC Málaga and later shared gameplay footage on social media. When the group stops at a hot spring, they'll benefit from a permanent increase to their max HP. The health bonus and moments shared between each character seem to be the real draw. The thing that might appeal to some players more than others, though, is the promise that the bathing suit outfits featured during these segments can be unlocked as skins, too.
【名湯めぐりの旅🐤】 冒険の合間に、ほっとひと息。 #FF7リベレーション のワールドマップに隠された温泉スポット♨旅の仲間たちとのここでしか聞けない特別な会話が楽しめます。さらに最大HPアップの効果や衣装スキンが手に入ることも https://t.co/S41hqabFqp

Across all of the clips shown online today, we can see skins for Cloud, Barret, and Cid. Red XIII can relax in the hot springs, too, but considering he's not usually wearing clothes to begin with, it doesn't look like any skin he may get will change his appearance too much. Then, there's newly playable party member Vincent Valentine, who prefers to bathe in the same slick get-up he fights monsters in because he's… just that cool, I guess.

"We’re sharing a preview of some of the hot spring events revealed during our stage presentation at SDCC Málaga," director Naoki Hamaguchi said in a follow-up post on X/Twitter. "Each hot spring offers a different glimpse into the characters’ everyday lives, and the outfits featured in these events can also be unlocked as skins. Explore the world, discover hot springs, and enjoy these special moments with your companions!"

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is still months from delivering the concluding chapter of the remake trilogy, but that hasn't stopped Square Enix from unloading new details as often as it can manage. Hamaguchi has been especially keen to share, telling IGN last month that players will have an option to automatically level up their characters if they want to skip the grind. He's also said players could easily spend more than 100 hours playing through the story , even if the Platinum Trophy doesn't present much of a challenge on its own .

Final Fantasy 7 Revelation launches for PC, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S April 8, 2027. While we wait to see how those hot springs heat things up for Cloud and company, you can see how Hamaguchi responded to players hoping for a full-disc release . You can also check out IGN's hands-on preview .

items.title: 《神秘海域 5》传闻中，内森·德雷克演员表示他会回归，但有一个条件
items.summary: One of actor Nolan North's most famous roles is that of Nathan Drake in Naughty Dog's Uncharted franchise, but

content.v: One of actor Nolan North's most famous roles is that of Nathan Drake in Naughty Dog's Uncharted franchise, but he wrapped things up with 2016's Uncharted 4: A Thief's End. There are rumors that Naughty Dog is making a new Uncharted game , and North has said he would "110%" be up for coming back in a new game in the storied series.

“110%. Absolutely. I think it would be one of the biggest games ever if they decided to do it. It just depends if Sony wants to make money," he said at Gamergy in Puerto Rico prior to the recent rumors of Uncharted 5 ( via DomTheBomb ). "I absolutely would. I try to stay in shape just in case. I can't see a scenario where I would say no. I always keep out hope."
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Screenshot-2026-10-05-at-2.50.05-PM.png
North went on to clarify that he has not heard anything about a new Uncharted game where he might be asked to come back, but he thinks it would be a good business decision for Sony.
"It is a business-my god, can you imagine if they did? It would be the biggest announcement in gaming. I don't think that's hyperbole. I think that's true," he said.
North said he enjoyed working with Naughty Dog over the years on the four main Uncharted games, and that's part of why he would be up to come back.

His one caveat, however, is that he hopes Naughty Dog wouldn't make something that doesn't live up to the franchise's legacy. He cited Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull as an example of a middling movie in an otherwise great series, and he doesn't want that to happen for Uncharted.

According to multiple sources, a fifth mainline Uncharted game will be Naughty Dog's next project after Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet , which is reportedly due for release in 2027. A third The Last of Us game could follow after.

Intriguingly, the report said Nathan Drake would appear in the hypothetical Uncharted 5 in some capacity. Uncharted 4 was positioned as the definitive end for Nathan Drake’s story when it released in 2016, but Naughty Dog has repeatedly suggested that it is not done with the franchise .
When Uncharted 5 might release is anyone’s guess, but it’s more likely that it’ll arrive on the PlayStation 6 given that Sony is expected to release its next-generation console sometime in 2028.
North played Nathan Drake in the four main Uncharted games, but not The Lost Legacy. He had a cameo in the Uncharted movie, too.

items.title: Physint 更新：小岛秀夫分享了有关他即将推出的《合金装备》精神继任者的新信息
items.summary: Renowned game director Hideo Kojima revived his Koji10 podcast after a year and shared casting, story, and dev

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/05/physint-1758605986884-1791225805552.jpg

Renowned game director Hideo Kojima revived his Koji10 podcast after a year and shared casting, story, and development updates on Physint, his upcoming next-generation action-espionage game and spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid.

Thanks to a summary of the 79-minute English-subtitled podcast on YouTube by X user Genki_JPN, we now know a bit more about the status of Physint, which made huge headlines recently after Kojima revealed that Sony was set to cancel the project as its publisher, leading to Microsoft picking it up . Kojima describes Physint as a project to commemorate his 40th anniversary as a game developer. He said he wants it to evoke the roots of the Metal Gear Solid games, but be a new interactive experience with a different kind of spy action. He aims to fill it with lots of new ideas.

Story and cast-wise, Kojima says he has the plot already and that he pitched all of the actors appearing in it himself – 70% of whom are apparently Kojima fans. Many of the character names have been decided Filming will start next year, with Bill Skarsgard , Charlie Fraser and Minami Hamabe already scanned.
Finally, the 63-year-old Kojima said that he makes every one of his games as if it could be his last.
The other game Kojima is developing for Microsoft, the PT spiritual successor OD, is expected to be released before Physint, which Kojima himself said was 5-6 years away last year.

items.summary: Gears of War: E-Day rolls out worldwide starting October 6, and thanks to early access players, The Coalition

content.v: Gears of War: E-Day rolls out worldwide starting October 6, and thanks to early access players, The Coalition has identified several issues that it's fixing with the game's first patch. Focused mostly on overall stability and performance across the game's campaign, multiplayer, and Horde Siege modes, the Gears of War: E-Day update is out now.

One of the biggest fixes is the "Bilefrog-Kalona" error, an issue named after the gigantic subterranean Locust frogs encountered throughout the game, which regularly try to kill you by vomiting stomach acid at your position. Nasty stuff. The Coalition assigned several Gears-themed names to its network errors, and in this case, getting vomit-frogged is a specific split-screen multiplayer issue. This triggers when a split-screen player is automatically signed out of online services after the console or PC is suspended, then tries to use Quick Resume to hop back in.

The Coalition says it has also addressed an issue in Versus Social matches that results in players entering a waiting-lobby limbo, and fixed an issue that could prevent certain Siege Blitz Secure objectives from being completed. For the campaign, several pesky problems across Act 2 are being patched, while other game-wide instances of sticky turrets and unearned War Journal progress have been resolved.

These fixes come on the eve of the game's worldwide rollout on PC and Xbox Series X|S, and an influx of Game Pass subscribers are expected to enter Kalona starting tomorrow. While the overall story isn't the best Gears of War narrative, the game is still recommended for anyone who wants a big, dumb, and loud cover-based shooter that looks gorgeous on PC and Xbox Series X|S.

"For better or worse, E-Day is distinctly Gears, and I had a good time with it, even if the story is disappointing and the open areas are fairly dull," Richard Wakeling wrote in GameSpot's Gears of War: E-Day campaign review . "But that’s all it is: a good game, propped up by combat that hasn’t changed all that much over the past 20 years. That’s enough to skate by, but I wish Gears of War would dig deeper."

items.title: 为什么 GTA Studio 联合创始人避开 GTA 6 以及所有开放世界游戏
items.summary: Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser left the company in 2020 and now runs a new outfit called Absurd Ventures. Hous

content.v: Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser left the company in 2020 and now runs a new outfit called Absurd Ventures. Houser will be forever connected to the GTA franchise, and he's now weighed in on GTA 6 .
He told Variety that he did not watch the "Extended Look" trailer and doesn't plan to. Why? He said he tries to avoid consuming things that are going to "disrupt me creatively."

"And given that I spend a large amount of time trying to make open-world games, and the rest of my conscious time trying to figure out innovative ways to market them, I don’t need to see what other people are [doing]," he said. "I’m always trying to think about new ways of doing it, not sit there in some kind of comparison of what I would have done differently.”
Also in the interview, Houser said he doesn't play a lot of open-world games anymore, for similar reasons.

"I find when I play them, I can almost deconstruct the strengths and weaknesses of the team in real time and it’s distracting. I’m always thinking, ‘Well, their animation team is weak, but I think this game design is fantastic.’ And, ‘Oh, I can imagine that meeting when they discuss this feature,'" he said. "I’m not a game designer; I’m a sort of creative director. So I’m trying to always find new things that haven’t been done before, or that I can steal from older media, quite frankly or just inspired me or things I always thought about.”
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/GTA6-Large-1.jpeg
It's not that Absurd Ventures is burying its head in the sand, however. Houser went on to say he has a team of people at his company who take the time to examine "what everyone else is doing."

He said when Rockstar began to develop Red Dead Redemption, he avoided watching any more Western films. For GTA, he said he avoided HBO's acclaimed mob show The Sopranos (1999-2007) because "it would have disrupted everything I did on GTA" if he had seen the show while formulating the GTA series, which was first released in 1997.
"So I really try and avoid things that I think are going to overly influence me," he said.

Houser is now working on multiple projects at Absurd Ventures, including an open-world comedy game that he will reveal further "in the next few months." Another is a dystopian sci-fi game about "video game development gone very wrong" when a rogue AI becomes sentient.

He said in the Variety interview that "there could be no greater compliment" than to be forever associated with GTA. At the same time, Houser said he hopes some of what he works on at Absurd Venture can be successful in its own right.

Dan Houser's brother and Rockstar co-founder, Sam Houser, remains at Rockstar and was involved in the creation of GTA 6. GQ writer Sam White recently posted a series of tweets (and then deleted them) saying an interview he had planned with Sam Houser fell apart at the last minute . That's notable because Sam Houser rarely gives any interviews at all, nor does he appear in Rockstar's official promotional efforts for the company's releases.
GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. In other news, Rockstar recently revealed some of its secrets and detailed how a game like GTA 6 gets made .

items.title: 开发者更新 | 10.2.0 PTB 实时更改
items.summary: With the release of 10.2.0 just around the corner, we wanted to take some time to talk to you about a handful

content.v: With the release of 10.2.0 just around the corner, we wanted to take some time to talk to you about a handful of the many changes that will be happening from PTB to the Live release - and a few changes that won’t. We want to thank everyone who took the time during the PTB to share their thoughts, as we always take your feedback very seriously when it comes time to make these changes.
Shoulder the Burden
Removed the deactivation condition for other Survivors.

Dev note: We understand your concerns around the impact of the condition of this perk deactivating after one use for all Survivors for solo players who cannot communicate. Therefore, we have removed this limitation.
This is Not Happening
Removed the Great basic Skill Check zone increase.
Dev note: We noticed the concerns about This is Not Happening when combined with Hyperfocus, and as a result have decided to remove the great basic skill check zone.
Dark Arrogance
Basic-attack cooldown no longer affects successful hits.

Dev note: We saw your feedback that Killers were recovering from attacks – including successful hits – too quickly on the PTB, which ended up making chases feel too short. One of the key culprits of that was Dark Arrogance. The cooldown on the PTB was ultimately doing too much by including successful hits, so it now only affects missed and obstructed attacks.
Windows of Opportunity – will remain the same as PTB

Dev note: While we understand that there were many concerns about this change impacting newer players, we do believe that Windows was doing too much and overshadowing other perks, so we will be keeping these changes. We hope that making other Survivor perks more useful will make up for this, even with different activation conditions – such as Dark Sense.
Borrowed Time – will remain the same as it currently is on Live
Dev note: We’ve reverted Borrowed Time back to its Live iteration. While we liked what we explored, we didn’t like that we were removing a useful anti-tunnel option, so old Borrowed Time is back.
While we have many more changes coming for the release, we wanted to take this time to address the loudest concerns ahead of time. Keep an eye out tomorrow for the full set of Patch Notes.
Until next time…
The Dead by Daylight Team

items.title: 使用 SSD 作为 RAM，《战争机器：E-Day》在 Xbox Series S 上流畅运行
items.summary: The Coalition was able to work some magic on the Xbox Series S by tapping into the SSD to increase performance

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/01/btfiuoeldu6mkzuez7e008xhvd1icgg-jcb-u5aiuoy-1790813782471.jpeg

While Gears of War: E-Day is a beautiful game, it's incredibly demanding, whether you're playing it on the Xbox Series X or on PC. But, The Coalition was able to work some magic on the Xbox Series S by tapping into the SSD to increase performance.

The Coalition's studio technical director Kate Raynor talked to Digital Foundry and described tapping into the SSD while the Series S was out of memory. That's important for a game as demanding as Gears of War: E-Day, as the Xbox Series S only has 10GB of RAM, rather than the 16GB on the Series X.

Offloading data from the RAM to an SSD is nothing new. Your computer does it all the time when you run out of memory. What happens then is that the computer relies on the Page File, a dedicated block of storage on your SSD or hard drive that's used to hold overflow data. The problem with relying on that typically, though, is that SSDs are way slower than RAM, which is why your computer slows to a halt whenever it has to lean on the Page File.

The key for Gears of War: E-Day, then, was strategically choosing which data to offload to the SSD, and which data to keep in the faster system memory. According to Digital Foundry, The Coalition got around this by prioritizing data that wasn't used "in a frame or over a run of frames," while data that's constantly needed stays in RAM.

This approach does have its limits, though, and will degrade performance over time if the page file is refreshed into memory too often – as that does have a performance cost on its own. But, with this memory trick and dropping Lumen reflections, The Coalition was able to get Gears of War: E-Day running pretty well on the Xbox Series S. Hopefully, more developers are able to adopt this approach going forward, because I have a feeling that the cheaper hardware in the Xbox Series X is going to be more necessary as the RAM crisis carries on.

Gears of War: E-Day launched last week into early access, and has some pretty big changes over past games. But, still, The Coalition is proud that Gears of War: E-Day is now one of Xbox's main exclusives.

items.title: 我在侠盗猎车手 5 中以瞪羚的优雅嬉戏
items.summary: More than usual, I mean.

content.v: I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier .

La Rochefoucauld once wrote, "What grace is to the body, good sense is to the mind." He wrote this some time before the release of Grand Theft Auto 5 , and was likely referring to Mirror's Edge instead.

Regardless, it holds true today. And you know what? Whatever their qualities, the gentlemen of GTA 5 simply don't have much grace to them. They are lumpy, ambling figures, and move like young children unused to their bulk. I have rectified this using Back Flip Mod —a mod for back flip. "Simple backflip for Single Player," it says, with an alarmingly cavalier attitude to capitalisation and style-guide coherence.

But it's true. Now, with a tap of page down (enormous shoutout to the author for choosing page down, by the way: one of few keys left on my keyboard not already colonised by another mod) the lads of Los Santos will, whimsically, backflip in place. Then they'll get very pleased with themselves for pulling it off.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/24pAGiiFbVVmKYZ3CdRyun-1920-80.gif

"There's a chance the backflip fails and your character ragdolls," notes the mod's author, which is delicious. Of course, in my testing so far, failures happen not mid-backflip but more at the conception of the backflip idea.

That is to say, you hit the backflip button and—if the dice roll deems it to be a failure—your character collapses immediately, without even moving. In fairness, many of my own ideas and impulses fail in precisely the same way.

items.title: 小岛秀夫让《OD》保持神秘，以使其恐怖效果更加强烈
items.summary: Games developed by Hideo Kojima typically have an air of mystery, but for his upcoming horror project OD , the

content.v: Games developed by Hideo Kojima typically have an air of mystery, but for his upcoming horror project OD , the veteran game director wants to both terrify and mystify his fans. On a new episode of his weekly radio show Koji10, Kojima briefly spoke about the game, avoiding the release of teasers, and ensuring that players get a proper shock when playing it

"It's still a mystery. That doesn't mean we haven't made the game," Kojima said. "I want to keep quiet and release it. That's unusual for me, isn't it? I normally put out teaser after teaser. This time I don't want to reveal much. A mystery. It's so new that it's a mystery. It aims to create a new experience and test the limits of what players can bear in terms of fear. The limits of fear, that's the idea behind the title. The critical point of fear."

OD was originally announced in 2023 , with the game being described as an experiment on what it means to overdose on fear--hence the title, OD. As for Kojima's comments about marketing, the first Death Stranding was a prime example: There were several teaser trailers and extended gameplay previews, each leaving viewers with more questions than answers. Kojima isn't even sure OD will find an audience , as he believes the gameplay systems are unlike anything he's created in his career.

Alongside his Metal Gear Solid spiritual successor Physint , Xbox is supporting development on OD, and the game is reportedly safe from the studio closures, layoffs, and game cancellations that have hit Microsoft's gaming division throughout 2026.

The game features actors Hunter Schafer and Sophia Lillis, although it's unclear how much of a role the late Udo Kier will have in OD, following his death last year . Kojima previously said that the 2025 SAG-AFTRA strike forced the team to reschedule filming for OD until 2026, although Kier can still be seen in the early teaser for OD.

items.title: 日本传奇蛇演员想要一款新的《合金装备》游戏，但“没有小岛就不会做一款游戏”
items.summary: Solid Snake's legendary Japanese actor is keen to return for a new game, though feels conflicted about any fre

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2025/08/29/snake-1756488499862.jpg
Solid Snake's Japanese voice and motion capture actor is keen to return for a new game, though feels conflicted about any fresh entry without the involvement of creator Hideo Kojima.

In an interview with Bunshun (translated by IGN), Snake actor Akio Otsuka reminisced about his deep attachment to the Metal Gear series and keen desire for Konami to make another entry — which may come as a surprise for Japanese fans of the series. Famously, Otsuka previously said he wouldn’t make a new game sans Kojima — a quote that spread around the franchise's Japanese fandom after the Konami/Kojima split.

Reflecting on that and his bond with the series' creator, Otsuka said: "My job as a voice actor is to do what I’m told. But when it comes to the Metal Gear series, it was created by Kojima, and I take pride in having helped bring it to life.
"So I [previously] said, 'I don’t want to do a Metal Gear that doesn’t involve Kojima.' Now I've said that, I can't take it back," he said.

Given Konami and Hideo Kojima’s far from amicable split, it seems pretty unlikely that Kojima will ever helm a MGS game again. When asked whether Otsuka had told Kojima that he’d like the Death Stranding director to make a new Metal Gear game, Otsuka simply replied: "I'll leave that to your imagination."

Looking back over his years of voicing Snake, Otsuka recalled that Solid Snake's famous "Kept you waiting, huh?" (" mataseta na" ) line was actually an adlib during the Japanese language recording. "It was subsequently used in ads too," Otsuka added, with David Hayter’s English rendition of the line becoming equally iconic.

Otsuka also recalled how surreal it was to have his real-life father, voice actor Chikao Otsuka, voicing Big Boss in MGS4’s finale, while Otsuka himself provided the performance capture. "When I arrived on set, my father's eyes widened at the sight of me in the motion capture suit, and he asked with surprise, 'Am I actually going to be voicing you?' It was rather amusing."

Otsuka expressed much fondness and empathy for Kojima throughout the interview. "He went through so many difficulties after leaving Konami yet managed to finish making this major game," Otsuka said, referring to the creator's subsequent project, Death Stranding. "After all, if Death Stranding had failed he could have easily ended up with debts that he wouldn't have been able to pay off even if he continued working for the rest of his life… So when the game was finished and they announced its release, I burst into tears."

Otsuka has also previously expressed support for former members of Kojima's team still working at Konami, who for various reasons did not jump ship to Kojima’s new company Kojima Productions. In an MGS cutscene-worthy bit on his Nameless Mouse podcast back in June 2023, Otsuka emphasized that, "I want the fans to understand this. I don't want them [the remaining MGS staff at Konami] to be made out to be villains. The people who stayed at Konami were part of the crew on Kojima's ship. These people, who inherited the director's legacy, want to protect Metal Gear."

Just as David Hayter is commonly held up by MGS fans as the definitive English voice of Snake (despite his controversial replacement by Kiefer Sutherland in MGS5), Otsuka's performance holds similar significance for Japanese fans. "I certainly have a deep attachment to Snake," Otsuka concluded. "After all, to the [Japanese] fans, Snake will always be Akio Otsuka, regardless of what happened between Kojima and Konami. When I think of the fans… well I'm really caught in the middle.”

While Kojima may be busy for the foreseeable future working on new projects O.D. and Physint, Konami clearly still has an interest in Metal Gear — something that may well lead to an all-new entry in future. Last year's successful Metal Gear Solid Delta Snake Eater reused Otsuka’s original performance from 2006's MGS3. However, it seems that the actor might be open to working on a new Metal Gear Solid, should Konami choose to make more than just remasters and remakes of the groundbreaking stealth series.

items.title: 开发商有点太傻了，推荐在其坏男孩主题鸡尾酒中添加致命的精神活性成分
items.summary: Maybe a little *too* bad, LaDS?

content.v: Fun, thematic videogame recipes are not new. Suggesting dangerous and potentially lethal ingredients, however? Well, Love and Deepspace might just be the first game to make such a bold move.

Yes, Infold's hunky dating gacha recently posted to X with a handful of fun cocktails themed around the male suitors you can romance. Something worth noting here is that each one has a signature flower associated with them—childhood friend Caleb is the crabapple blossom, Xavier has the forget-me-not, and doctor Zayne is the jasmine. These are not the flowers that are the issue.

Shake, swirl... and take a sip! One taste of this Special Blend🍸️ and you won't forget it.Exotic Fruits picked together are blended into a taste of happiness.A little of this, a little of that, and one last must-have ingredient...?🍸️What secret ingredient would you add to this Special Blend made just for him?🎁Feel free to post with the hashtag #SleeplessBanquet or share in the comments. You can share text, screenshots, or photos!We will randomly select 5 Hunters to receive a redeem code for [Diamond*100, Stamina*100, and Gold*10,000]!———🪐Official Discord: https://t.co/hKmnBAbbgu🪐Download and Log in Now: https://t.co/bNEP8yM6bZ#LoveandDeepspace #ANightThatNeverEnds September 29, 2026

The problematic posies in question come from the game's other two romantic interests, Rafayel and Sylus—whose signature flowers are the fire lily and datura respectively. They are, erm, quite toxic. And potentially even deadly. In the datura's case, it's also a psychoactive plant. Which makes it even more surprising that Infold deigned to include them as garnishes in these fun and funky cocktail recipes.

It took the developer a whopping 36 hours to post a follow-up tweet which read: "Safety notice: All drinks shown are fictional and for in-game purposes only. Do not attempt to recreate or consume them in reality." Of course, by this point, the original post had already been community noted and flooded with fans asking the very important question: "Hey, what the hell?"

I'm not sure I've ever seen a developer create thematic food and drink recipes with real ingredients that weren't meant to be recreated, which makes this whole situation even more bizarre. You can certainly create interesting cocktails for your characters that don't rely on a potentially deadly flower, and providing recipes people aren't even meant to follow begs the question of why Infold would even bother in the first place?
Let's just hope nobody ever lets Infold create one of those fandangled videogame cookbooks.

items.title: 神包正式登陆万智牌
items.summary: Magic: The Gathering booster packs have gone through a lot of changes in the last decade, some of which have b

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2023/07/13/mtg-lotr-1689261089706.png

Magic: The Gathering booster packs have gone through a lot of changes in the last decade, some of which have been awful. But Wizards of the Coast is introducing 'God Packs' to MTG, which could feel like winning the lottery.

Everyone who plays TCGs knows the rush you get when you open a booster with a better spread of rares and mythics than usual. Right now, in a Play Booster, that usually means getting between two and four rares and mythics, and it feels incredible when it happens. But in a blog post , Wizards is taking that feeling a step further by announcing 'God Packs,' which will be entirely comprised of rares and mythics.

Both Play Boosters and Collector Boosters will have a chance to be a god pack, with Collector Boosters naturally being way more likely to hit gold. Approximately 1 in 1,000 Play Boosters will be God Packs, and 1 in 300 Collector Boosters will be God Packs.

God Packs will have their loot distributed differently between Play and Collector boosters, too. For Play boosters, you'll get one special 'God Pack celebration card' – whatever that means – along with 10 non-foil Rares and Mythics. Then, there will be two non-foil 'Booster Fun' variants (think showcase and borderless cards), along with two foil 'Booster Fun' cards.

For Collector Boosters, though, you'll get one foil land, 3 foil default frame rares and/or mythics, 3 non-foil 'Booster Fun' variants, and 5 foil 'Booster Fun' variants. On top of these rare God Packs, though, Wizards says in its blog, "while we're at it, we're also increasing the drop rates on foil rare and mythic rare cards across booster packs" in order to make them more fun to open.

But it can't all be fun and games; Wizards is also removing things from boosters, like foil commons and uncommons from play boosters altogether. It's also trimming the amount of cards in Collector Boosters down to 12, by removing 3 of the foil common and uncommon slots.
Wizards claims that these changes will make opening Collector Boosters more meaningful, saying in its blog:

"How does removing cards make opening Collector Boosters more exciting? We'll be honest here—it doesn't. But we do know that most people who open Collector Boosters mostly skip past these cards. Not everyone, but enough of a majority. You can see it in virtually any Collector Booster opening video, where the video practically skips over that section of the booster. Removing them isn't about shrinking the experience; it's about making room—in terms of both printing capacity and player psychology—for cards people actually get excited about."

There are a lot of people who skip through their commons and uncommons when cracking a lot of packs, hell I do it sometimes. But there are enough commons and uncommons that see constructed play and already jump in price – just look at Aetherdrift's Stock Up – that I could see removing these uncommon slots having unforseen consequences.

Either way, these booster changes will go live when Nauctis: The Sunken Realm, and will carry over to every in-universe set going forward. As for Universes Beyond, those sets will get these new booster changes starting in 2028.

items.title: 像 GTA 6 这样的游戏实际上是如何制作的？ Rockstar 的做法如下
items.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the most highly anticipated game releases this year, or ever. The fran

content.v: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the most highly anticipated game releases this year, or ever. The franchise is known for its massive scope and impressive attention to detail, but how is a game like GTA 6 actually made? In a new interview with Love magazine ( via Kotaku ), Rockstar North boss Rob Nelson said that part of the secret sauce with the GTA franchise is that many of its developers have been working together for a long time and have a "good sense of what they need to do."
In terms of actually building the game, Nelson said the process begins by creating assets and systems, and then "roughing in content across all areas of development."

More specifically, Nelson said GTA 6 was built through a series of eight-week milestones where select pieces of the game are compiled together. Then, the team evaluates those pieces, incorporates changes based on feedback, and then gets back to work on the next milestone.

"We work our way there, year after year, one obsessive day at a time, course-correcting as we go; always with the feeling we want the finished game to have firmly in mind, knowing that often we have to find that feeling, and trusting that, even if we haven’t found it yet, we will eventually," he said.

Another way Rockstar gets a game like GTA 6 out the door is by working with a lot of people. Anyone who watched the credits roll on Rockstar's last game, Red Dead Redemption II, is aware of just how many people worked on that game. For GTA 6, it wouldn't be surprising if the headcount is even higher.
GTA 6 writing director James Horton said, "There are no shortcuts when it comes to building a world like this."

“It’s a question of giving the right people the resources they need to build something that’s not only vast and varied as a whole, but where every part rings true no matter how small it is, or how closely you look at it," he said. "It needs to wash over you when you’re sprinting down the busiest street in the city, hearing snatches of a hundred different conversations as you go; and it needs to be totally convincing if you decide to stop and pay close attention to any one of those conversations."
Rockstar spun up a team in Los Angeles to work exclusively on NPCs, to help them feel more alive.

"Every room in the game, somebody thought about this," Rockstar's Aaron Garbut told The New York Times . "Who's sitting where, what they're drinking, the marks that are left on the table. The pictures on the wall will have the people that are in that room, with their tattoos on their arms and their family behind them. That whole thing has been made, and built, and photographed, and placed in this random room in a random building in a huge city, in a world."
Rockstar's developers also visited strip clubs in Florida and did ride-alongs with police to help get the details right in its recreation of Miami for Vice City.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. After a long period of silence, Rockstar has finally begun to reveal more details and show the game off. For lots more, be sure to read all of the new things we just learned about GTA 6 .

items.title: 比尔·斯卡斯加德如何成为小岛秀夫 Physint 的代言人
items.summary: Hideo Kojima's spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid, Physint , doesn't just have a new home at Xbox ; it al

content.v: Hideo Kojima's spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid, Physint , doesn't just have a new home at Xbox ; it also has a famous face attached to it, with Bill Skarsgard (It, Boy Kills World) playing the lead role. Thanks to Death Stranding 2: On the Beach composer Yoann "Woodkid" Lemoine, Kojima was introduced to Skarsgard, who would later be cast as the yet-to-be-named protagonist of Physint.

"He's been in some excellent films. Directors I know have worked with him and can't praise him enough," Kojima said on a new episode of the Koji 10 radio program. "I wanted to work with him for a long time. Then one day, Bill visited Woodkid's studio. When Bill went to his studio, he saw piles of Kojima Productions merchandise. He said, 'What's this? Why do you have all this!?' Yoann said, 'I worked with them,' and that’s how Yoann introduced us."
Kojima would later travel to Sweden to meet Skarsgard and his family. Skarsgard was a fan of the Metal Gear franchise, and Kojima pitched him the lead role in Physint, which Skarsgard accepted.

It's still early days for Physint, and Kojima says that Skarsgard is eager to get his hands on the game's script so that he can start preparing for the role. "We've finished his scan now. We have to scan actors early, because processing the data takes a long time," Kojima explained. "We'll film the performance much later. But he's so eager he doesn't want to wait. He keeps asking me for the script. I have the plot ready. But he wants to know the lines and how his character speaks. He wants to start preparing now. He's really eager. That's how deeply he gets into a role.

One other crucial factor in choosing Skarsgard was his chemistry with his fellow Physint actor, Charlee Fraser. "The poster we released the other day showed him with Charlee. Their chemistry is very important," Kojima added. "We tested their on-screen chemistry and did a camera test. We scanned them in full makeup. Their clothes were just for reference; these aren't the final costumes. The contrast between these two is striking."

Skarsgard also kept his involvement secret, as Kojima added that not even his parents knew he was going to be the star of Physint. "He's so serious; he hadn’t told anyone. It was confidential, of course, since we hadn't announced it," Kojima added. "Even his parents didn't know. That's impressive. He's a very conscientious person."

Physint won't be out for a long time, but Kojima has said that it's the "biggest-selling" game that he could possibly create . With Skarsgard and several other actors attached, it's likely also a very expensive game to produce, with unconfirmed reports that Physint’s budget at Sony was over $400 million. This figure has never been confirmed, but it is rumored that Xbox is paying a lot less to get it over the finish line.

items.title: 《弧线突袭者》和《总决赛》正在被改编成电影和电视节目
items.summary: Hollywood is mining Arc Raiders and The Finals for its next big video game adaptations, as the two franchises

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/22/arc-raiders-expedition-delay-1787357374549.png
Hollywood is mining Arc Raiders and The Finals for its next big video game adaptations, as the two franchises will be turned into films and TV shows.

Per Variety , Nexon, the parent company of developer Embark Studios, will team up with a production company known as Chernin Entertainment to develop adaptations of Arc Raiders and The Finals. As of right now, it sounds like the teams are exploring all possible options, which include TV shows and films. This will be done to help expand the worlds of these games that "reward the passion" of the players, according to Nexon.

“ARC Raiders and The Finals are exactly the kind of opportunities we’ve been building towards at Chernin Entertainment: ambitious global IP with the potential to become major franchises across film and television,” said David Ready, president of film at Chernin Entertainment. “Nexon and Embark have created visually stunning, atmospheric worlds that contain countless stories to tell. We’re honored they’ve trusted us to unite our film and television teams to tell those stories.”

Embark Studios says it will work directly with Chernin Entertainment to develop these adaptations, ensuring there is respect paid to the worlds and lore that fans have fallen in love with over the years. As of right now, there are no release dates or specifics for these projects, so they are likely still years away from materializing.

Arc Raiders was one of the biggest games of 2025, but it has lost some steam in recent months due to a lack of steady updates with significant content. Later this month, Embark plans to test a PvE mode in the game , allowing players to enjoy a more cooperative experience without fear of being gunned down by other players. The studio emphasized that there's no guarantee that this mode will become permanent, but it is exploring the option following demand from players.

items.title: RuneScape 开发者在 RuneFest 首次亮相人工智能生成的六指角色后道歉：“这很难解释”
items.summary: Uh oh, here we go again.

content.v: RuneScape developer Jagex descended upon Birmingham (the British one, not the Alabama one) over the weekend with its annual RuneFest. As part of its RuneScape keynote, it showed off a trailer for its upcoming Dragon Slayer 2 quest which, er, featured a player character with six fingers and a bizarre sneaker-like sole on their very not- sneaker armoured shoes.

It didn't take long for posts on social media to point out what was undeniably generative AI, and an incident which, unfortunately for Jagex, came very swiftly after another genAI controversy surrounding its clothing collaboration with 100 Thieves just days before.

Despite the trailer being for RS3, Old School RuneScape's Alec 'Mod Sween' Sween took the lead on releasing a statement on the 2007scape subreddit addressing the situation. "We're aware of the concerns raised about the Dragon Slayer 2 trailer and have taken it down, while we investigate this urgently," he wrote. "This trailer was produced by a trusted external partner who had explicitly confirmed that GenAI would not be used. But, among other things, there's a sixth finger and, well, that's pretty hard to explain away. For that we apologise."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/7KH4pXEUarS6MAeWYZhEhX-1920-80.jpg

Similar to his statement after the 100 Thieves incident, Sween reiterated Jagex's stance. "Our position is clear at Jagex: we don't use GenAI to create our games, artwork or creative assets, and will not knowingly allow it to be used on our behalf. This is the second time in quick succession that concerns about generative AI have arisen through partners we trusted, and for us that highlights an issue with our own processes which we must address."

Sween said that the developer is "overhauling" the review process, and in the meantime will "work with and commission creators from the community to make sure that the story of Dragon Slayer 2 is told to the standard befitting of such an update."

I can't help but feel a little surprised that a video this blatantly riddled with generative AI slipped through the cracks—the six fingers are clear as day, even if you manage to miss everything else—and in a response Sween said that the team "should have caught these things," adding: "We didn't do well enough and can't simply place the blame elsewhere."
For Jagex's sake, I hope the phrase "bad things come in threes" does not also apply to generative AI videogame controversies.

items.title: Arc Raiders 正在寻找“更多方式来整合真实的人类表演”，从 Celeste 对《冰雪奇缘》的视觉大修开始
items.summary: Celeste's voice actor will now also be the face of the unofficial leader of Speranza.

content.v: Embark is doing some monumental spring cleaning in the lead up to its major Arc Raiders ' update Frozen Trail . There's been an overhaul to its anticheat approach , the news of a potential PvE test , and a change to loot hotspots . But amid all of this, we're also getting a rework to one of Speranza's most important residents: Celeste.

Diana Gardner has been the voice of Celeste, Speranza's de facto leader, since the beginning, but Stefan Strandberg, the chief creative officer at Embark, explained in a blog post how Celeste has "never fully represented the depth of Diana’s performance." As her "limited expressive capabilities" held the character back and broke immersion for players, failing to communicate "the stakes and stories we want to tell."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/nbcyTKP3ArxM2bmu682tgg-1920-80.jpg
"Sometimes high fidelity, dynamic facial expressions are important to anchor the gravity of the story, and this is something that has constrained us up to this point," Strandberg adds.

So, with this in mind, Embark has set about reworking Celeste, with Gardner becoming her new face. "This is the first time we have used full motion capture, including a more detailed and accurate face, that allows us to map expressions and emotion in more detail. This means that more of Diana’s performance and identity comes through the screen."

This does mean Celeste will look different on October 6 when Frozen Trail releases, but rest assured all "you’re watching is the authentic performance of an incredibly talented actor, the real Celeste on screen for the first time."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/qNK4ekSM84LdSaBFWKoyUB-1920-80.png

It won't just end here though, as this is the start of a new wave of visual reworks for Arc Raiders as the team also intends to take a look at other characters. "In future updates, we plan to bring more characters in line with their real-world actors," Strandberg explains. "Not only will this mean more faithful representations of actors, it’ll be felt by players themselves."

Arc Raiders has always had one of the most exceptional worlds to explore, but it has unfortunately fallen short when it comes to characters. They are by and large just quite dull , sure the designs kind of look cool, but they've have always just been quest giving machines rather than convincing citizens of a game. This is not helped by its use of AI when it comes to beefing up voicelines .

So it comes as no surprise that Embark is seeking to remedy this, by "finding more ways to integrate real human performances into every interaction". Because that is the only way to tell a successful and convincing story.

items.title: 龙与地下城：魔兽世界 – 您需要了解的一切
items.summary: Dungeons and Dragons: World of Warcraft was announced way back in July, as the first Universes Beyond release

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/03/342305-cn-copy-1791050958738.jpg

Dungeons and Dragons: World of Warcraft was announced way back in July, as the first Universes Beyond release for the storied tabletop RPG. And just like the MMO it's based on, D&D: World of Warcraft is absolutely massive.

But while this was the first Universes Beyond release for D&D, it’s nothing new for Wizards of the Coast, with the initiative driving a huge number of Magic: The Gathering sets over the last few years. But just like the scope of the Lord of the Rings set for MTG, Dungeons and Dragons: World of Warcraft is an absolutely massive expansion, and almost feels like an entire game unto itself.

Rather than just taking the easy way out and releasing a one-off story module, Wizards of the Coast packed its World of Warcraft expansion with enough lore, dungeons, and professions that it could feasibly take you years to try everything. But, unlike WoW on your desktop, you can choose exactly how your Azeroth story will play out.
A Whole World of Warcraft

World of Warcraft has been around for 22 years on its own, and the franchise as a whole has been around since 1994. Needless to say, there is a ton of lore and history baked into the world of Azeroth. And, a huge portion of it is built into D&D: World of Warcraft.

The entire world of Azeroth is described in the book, up to The War Within. And, just like the game, each zone has a rough level range that Wizards had in mind when designing them. As Game Designer Joey Haeck says, “WoW has a starting zone for Orcs in Durotar, so it makes sense for that to be a level 1-4 zone in D&D.” Likewise, endgame zones like Northrend (at least zones that used to be endgame zones) will be designed with high-level characters in mind.
Though, this is D&D, so it’s entirely possible to just shrug off these suggestions and build your own campaign the way you want to. Haeck says, “as usual, with D&D, the power is in your hands.”

However, the expansion is focused entirely on the planet of Azeroth itself. So you won’t find the likes of Argus, the Shadowlands or Draenor here, though you can rely on your own knowledge of those worlds. Luckily, Shadowlands and Warlords of Draenor are two of the most maligned WoW expansions in history, so I’m sure a lot of people won’t miss them too much. It does mean, though, that you might have to get creative to do a campaign in The Burning Crusade’s Outland – which is just a blown-up Draenor.

But it’s not just the geography of Azeroth. Wizards of the Coast also worked in all the major conflicts that have driven the story of WoW over the years. Principal Game Designer James Wyatt listed just a few examples, like the Alliance vs. Horde campaign, the invasion of the Burning Crusade and the Scourge. The Dungeon Master’s guide will suggest you pick three of these conflicts to shape your campaign, which will then help populate the world with appropriate monsters, adventure hooks and locations.

In order to make out-of-order campaigns make sense, Wizards worked in a brilliant reference to the game to explain it: Chromie Time. As Wyatt describes, Chromie will tell you, "Look, I made a timeline just for you!”

I asked Wyatt a little more about the Chromie Time setup and he told me, “The campaign I’m playing in right now (which Joey Haeck is DMing) began with us in Silvermoon City having just helped repel Xal’atath’s invasion, but then Chromie sent us back in time to the Classic era, where we might or might not change the course of history!”
How Dungeons and Raids Work

One of the biggest parts of World of Warcraft is its dungeons and raids. And, of course, D&D: World of Warcraft is going to work those in, too. But, between D&D and World of Warcraft, dungeons are completely different types of gameplay. In the video game, you typically go in, barrel through all of the trash, nuke the boss down, loot and repeat. That doesn’t really fit Dungeons and Dragons’ gameplay.

Instead, the dungeons in D&D: WoW are environments where you’re expected to take things much more slowly. Rather than blowing everything up, these dungeons will have non-linear exploration, and you might need to talk your way out of situations, rather than relying on your DPS rotation. You might use stealth to just sneak past all the pirates in the Deadmines, rather than killing all of them.

Haeck describes some of the different ways players could tackle the Scarlet Monastery: “A sneaky party would have legends told about them, about how the Scarlet Crusade’s leadership vanished without a trace one day.”
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/03/342327-cn-copy-1791043448000.jpg

In Dire Maul, the book gives a brief history of the dungeon, about how the ancient Night Elf ruin was overrun by Satyrs and Ogres after the Well of Eternity exploded and Fel magic corrupted the mages who lived there. The book also has a couple of example adventure hooks, where you can either go in and kill Tendris Warpwood, like you do in the actual WoW dungeon, or you can take a quest from an Ogre to install a new king.

Unlike the video game, though, there’s not much fundamentally different between dungeons and raids. After all, Wizards of the Coast isn’t going to expect you to round up 20 or 40 people for a campaign. What are raids in WoW are instead dungeons geared for high-level players, with epic boss fights. The example Wizards gave is Onyxia’s Lair – a classic dungeon from Vanilla WoW, which basically only consists of one long hallway that leads to Onyxia herself.

Each of the dungeons in D&D: WoW seem like they have infinite possibilities, and luckily the book will have a lot of them. Wizards of the Coast didn’t reveal every dungeon in the game quite yet, but the ones it did reveal look incredible.
The dungeons so far:
Putting the Dragons in Dungeons & Dragons

Of course, the other side of D&D is the dragons, and those magical flying lizards play a huge role in both the tabletop game and World of Warcraft. But, while there are definitely similarities between the two, dragons in WoW are different to how they’re portrayed in D&D. For instance, Game Designer and Writer Carl Sibley described how he tackled the design of the Blue Dragons in D&D WoW.

“One of the cool things about WoW dragons is that they hold very distinct places in lore from the places in lore that D&D dragons hold," Sibley says. "So even though there’s a red dragon in WoW, a blue dragon, and a green dragon, they’re very different than the red, blue and green dragons in D&D for instance.”

With that different lore, comes different abilities, too. For instance, while blue dragons in WoW have a similar affinity to cold damage to White dragons in Dungeons & Dragons, the Blue Dragonflight on Azeroth are also masters of the Arcane. So, Sibley describes a blue dragon’s breath attack as both dealing cold damage, but also producing an aura that’ll interrupt spellcasters.

It’s not just dragons, though. D&D: WoW’s bestiary is vast, and it covers everything from Murlocs and Imps to the Lich King, all with the same level of detail and separated by challenge rating. Naturally, Murlocs are CR1 and Arthas is CR25, and should pose a significant challenge.

items.title: 《龙与地下城：魔兽世界》已经是一款出色的游戏，但正是它捕捉 MMO 精神的方式使其脱颖而出
items.summary: The tabletop adaptation of Blizzard's MMO drops next month.

content.v: Despite the immense volume of similarities between Dungeons & Dragons and World of Warcraft, the team working on the upcoming collab rulebook knows that you can't translate everything 1:1. Half of the MMO is about fighting the same bosses over and over until you finally get a good piece of loot. The grind isn't made for tabletop players.

During a recent presentation attended by PC Gamer, principal game designer and project lead James Wyatt says D&D: WoW is more about "paraphrasing" the MMO within the framework of the tabletop game rather than trying to emulate its mechanics. The entire world of Azeroth and the MMO's many expansions (up to Midnight) are fair game for players—the book opens with a big temporal hand-wave from time dragon Chromie—but the smallest details have been shuffled around to fit the format.

Popular dungeons from WoW's past, like the Deadmines, are mostly intact, save for a few alternate routes to accommodate parties who might want to sneak around bosses or skip some altogether. You're still in for the kinds of adventures through deep caverns and ancient cities that WoW players reminisce about today. Some dungeons are lifted right from WoW's earliest era, while others mix in their revised layouts (and loot) from later expansions.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/bes9keFSxVKmx4F8PNh8UQ-1920-80.jpg

I was delighted to hear that you can still take on the challenge of avoiding every boss in Dire Maul for the bonus rewards after you slay the king, otherwise known as a "tribute run" to WoW veterans. D&D: WoW is built to capture the spirit of exploring the MMO's dungeons for the first time, before the age of datamined loot tables and YouTube guides, while also letting you relive their most iconic moments at the table.

The team calls dungeons a toolbox for DMs to tell the stories of WoW's world without the trial-and-error of the MMO's combat or the tension of deciding who the blue dagger drop should go to. Enemy encounters are curated and there are no restrictions on taking a rest or leaving and coming back later—although the dangers can grow while you're away.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/yYtcwy4HuLGUkEfQWw4osQ-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/i5QwamBfd3sUi2dwc5dZqQ-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/fGeZkNtY69UQEiQz7GbJqQ-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/CajLvamw6q2rrP7paZZrjQ-1920-80.jpg

Climactic battles with WoW's biggest names are in there, too, including the Lich King, Illidan, Jaina Proudmoore, and more. They're also where you'll see some of the biggest changes from the MMO. Jaina, for example, doesn't gradually chill your party during the fight, but freezes a player and strikes them with an ice lance if you don't find a way to thaw them out fast enough (the devs recommend using fire, if you've got it) instead.

On the way to the dungeons, you'll have opportunities to prepare your party through WoW's gathering and crafting professions. D&D's crafting rules didn't require a ton of changes to make this work, the team says. You'll be able to do a wisdom check for supplies or ore to mine as you explore. You can take that ore and craft items from a list of recipes, provided you're proficient with the right tools. Powerful items, like armor, will be gated by your proficiency bonus, so there's a real incentive to keep improving your skills as you go along.

D&D's renown system also isn't that far off from WoW's faction reputation system, so the team kept it fairly straightforward: You earn rewards as you climb up the ranks of trust. Becoming exalted with the Earthen Ring can unlock a charm that lets you summon a big Elemental minion or a portal to teleport across the world. The dragon aspects, WoW's oldest and most powerful factions, will even grant you the equivalent of a Wish spell if they like you enough. Rival factions, where raising your reputation with one might damage the other, can show up, too.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/8U9JzkJy2Sh6zrF4zGpTQm-1920-80.jpg

Everything here sounds like a smart way to handle a collab that could've barely felt like a collab at all. WoW has so much overlap with D&D already that I can imagine a version of this book that just swaps some names around and calls it a day. Instead, you can tell this was created by people who know exactly what to pull out of Blizzard's world and what to leave behind.

We were told a lot more will be revealed in the lead up to the November 12 release, particularly the way classes from WoW map onto the tabletop format. Wyatt—who spent most of the presentation eagerly answering questions from chat—had to stop himself from spoiling things too early. He also says he's already thinking of all the leftover things that could fit into a follow-up book, but wants to see how this one goes before diving back into Azeroth.
